name: China
shortSummary: India and China maintain a heavily trade-linked but strategically adversarial relationship, dominated by an unresolved and heavily militarised Himalayan border and deep mutual distrust following the 2020 Galwan clash.
complexity: The 2020 Galwan Valley clash — the first fatal border confrontation in over four decades — froze high-level political engagement for years. Trade remains large and heavily imbalanced in China's favour even as troops remain forward-deployed along the Line of Actual Control.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: Both cooperate within BRICS, SCO and G20 despite bilateral friction.

majorChallenges.title: Unresolved Line of Actual Control
majorChallenges.description: The India-China border remains undemarcated across multiple sectors, with recurring stand-offs.

majorChallenges.title: Trade deficit
majorChallenges.description: India runs one of its largest bilateral trade deficits with China, concentrated in electronics and industrial inputs.

majorChallenges.title: China-Pakistan axis
majorChallenges.description: China's deep military and economic ties with Pakistan, including CPEC through Pakistan-administered Kashmir, are a persistent Indian concern.

recentDevelopments.title: Border patrolling agreement enables partial disengagement
recentDevelopments.description: India and China reached an agreement on patrolling arrangements at remaining friction points along the Line of Actual Control, enabling limited troop disengagement and a cautious resumption of some high-level contact.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: The first concrete de-escalation step since the 2020 Galwan clash, though large-scale troop deployments and mutual distrust persist.

recentDevelopments.title: Resumption of direct flights and limited people-to-people exchanges
recentDevelopments.description: Direct flight connectivity and some visa/exchange channels saw incremental easing as part of the broader post-2024 disengagement track.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: A modest normalization signal, though the underlying border dispute and trade imbalance remain unresolved.

historicalEvents.title: Panchsheel Agreement
historicalEvents.description: India and China sign an agreement enshrining five principles of peaceful coexistence, part of the "Hindi-Chini Bhai-Bhai" era.

historicalEvents.title: Sino-Indian War
historicalEvents.description: War breaks out over disputed Himalayan border territory; China declares a unilateral ceasefire after making significant advances, leaving lasting distrust.

historicalEvents.title: Rajiv Gandhi's Beijing Visit
historicalEvents.description: The first Indian prime ministerial visit to China since 1954 begins a normalization of ties.

historicalEvents.title: Doklam Standoff
historicalEvents.description: A 73-day military standoff near the Bhutan-China-India tri-junction after Indian troops halt Chinese road construction.

historicalEvents.title: Galwan Valley Clash
historicalEvents.description: A violent hand-to-hand clash in the Galwan Valley kills 20 Indian and an undisclosed number of Chinese soldiers — the first fatal India-China border incident since 1975.
historicalEvents.impact: Triggered a multi-year military stand-off, troop build-ups, and a freeze on high-level political visits; India banned dozens of Chinese mobile apps.

historicalEvents.title: Border Patrolling Agreement
historicalEvents.description: India and China reach an agreement on patrolling arrangements in remaining friction points, enabling a partial disengagement and resumption of some high-level contact.

agreements.name: Border Peace and Tranquility Agreement
agreements.description: Early confidence-building framework for managing the undemarcated border pending final settlement.

trade.majorImports: Electronics, machinery, active pharmaceutical ingredients, solar cells

multilateralRelations.detail: Joint founding member, cooperating on multilateral economic issues despite bilateral tension.
